subject: System Design
title: GraphQL: Ask for Exactly What You Need
description: A micro-lesson that makes GraphQL: Ask for Exactly What You Need usable.

hook.text: A REST API returns 50 fields when you only need 3. GraphQL lets you request exactly those 3.

buildup.text: GraphQL uses a single endpoint where clients specify the exact shape of data they want.

discovery.text: Facebook created GraphQL in 2012 to solve the problem of mobile apps over-fetching data.

twist.text: GraphQL reduces over-fetching but adds complexity: caching is harder and queries can be expensive.

climax.text: GraphQL shines when clients have diverse data needs. REST is simpler when they don't.

punchline.text: One query, exactly the data you need.

quiz.question: What problem did GraphQL originally solve?
options: Mobile apps over-fetching data from REST APIs
